Tagline: Artist creating sculptures and drawings that reflect on human interactions with nature in an urban setting.
Biography: Stephanie earned an M.F.A. from the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, a Post-Baccalaureate certificate from the School of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and a B.A. in Art History from the University of Virginia. She has presented solo exhibitions at the Wave Hill Sunroom Project Space and the Philadelphia International Airport, and two-person exhibitions at Florida State College, Jacksonville, FL and Musée d’art moderne André Malraux, Le Havre, France. Stephanie has participated in various artist residencies including I-Park Foundation in East Haddam, CT; an exchange program in Le Havre, France; the Artist Studios program at the Museum of Arts and Design in New York, NY; and Triangle Arts in Brooklyn, NY. Stephanie also completed a public art commission of a large wood mosaic for Makerpark in Staten Island, NY. She lives in Queens, NY and is a resident artist at ChaShaMa’s Space to Create in Brooklyn, NY.
Artist Statement:
I am inspired by the complexity of our relationship with the natural world, specifically trees. Most of my work focuses on human interventions with plants within an urban setting: exuberant cherry branches grafted onto pole-straight rootstock and street trees held up with poles and straps, or protected by rickety tree guards. My work considers how these practices of grafting, tying, and cutting on a larger scale can both destroy ecosystems and rejuvenate threatened species.

I work collaboratively with the plant material; the specific shape of each trunk or branch determines the form and narrative of the piece. The combination of milled wood and organic forms suggests prosthetics attempting to return a mechanically-altered material to its natural state, or conversely, as a mechanization of nature.

My work tends to be spare, highlighting line, form, and space to invite a close and quiet contemplation of the beauty of the natural world and how our actions affect it.

Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, Harman Center for the Arts, and at Smithsonian institutes, among other venues and festivals. Tagline: Self taught photographer specializing in people and representing them in the fullest authenticity
Artist Statement: Sean Chee is a self-taught Chinese American photographer who is passionate about people. He was born and raised in Queens, NYC, and still resides there to this day. He finds that much of the diversity of New York City bleeds into his work. It centers around the dialogue between him and his subjects, whether that be family, culture, or dreams. When approaching photography, he believes in communication and collaboration to fully breathe life into the photos. In his lifetime, he hopes to continue to learn more about himself through his love for photography and the world.

Tagline: Latinx art and design collective exploring relationships between people, place, and the more-than-human world.
Neighborhood_Map: Edgemere, Rockaway Beach, Arverne, Hammels, Neponsit
Biography:
Camila A. Morales is a Latinx interdisciplinary artist, designer, educator, and founder of Valé in Far Rockaway, New York. Working at the intersection of art, ecology, architecture, and new media, her practice explores the relationships between coastal environments, community, and storytelling through immersive installations, sound, public art, and participatory design. Rooted in her experience as a Chilean-Canadian immigrant, her work examines themes of place, belonging, environmental stewardship, and climate justice.

With over 15 years of experience spanning architecture, design, and the arts, Morales has contributed to the design and realization of internationally recognized cultural buildings, public artworks, and community-centered initiatives. She teaches at NYU Tandon School of Engineering and Parsons School of Design, where she mentors emerging artists and designers while integrating ecological thinking into their creative practice. Through Valé EcoLab, she leads free bilingual programs that foster environmental literacy, youth engagement, and creative approaches to coastal resilience in the Rockaways.
Artist Statement:
Valé is a Latinx-led eco-centered art and design collective baValé is a Latinx-led eco-centered art and design collective based in Far Rockaway, New York, founded by artist and educator Camila A. Morales. Our practice operates at the intersection of environmental justice, art, sound, and community-based research, using creative practice as a tool to deepen relationships between people, place, and the more-than-human world.

We work through deep listening and place-based inquiry, developing projects that translate ecological and cultural knowledge into shared experiences through public art, immersive installations, sonic archives, publications, and participatory workshops. Our methods combine bioacoustic recording, field research, microscopy, and creative technologies with community storytelling, creating spaces where residents become active participants in documenting and caring for their local environments.

Rooted in a frontline coastal community experiencing the impacts of climate change, our work centers those most affected by environmental change while celebrating the ecologies, histories, and everyday stories that shape the Rockaway Peninsula. Through free bilingual programming, youth workshops, and public art, we cultivate environmental literacy, ecological stewardship, and a deeper sense of belonging grounded in care for land, water, and one another.

The Valé EcoLab serves as a community space where artists, scientists, educators, and neighbors come together to explore, learn, and create. Through collaborative research and hands-on experimentation, we use art as a platform for environmental storytelling, collective knowledge sharing, and imagining more just and resilient futures.sed in Far Rockaway, New York, founded by artist and educator Camila A. Tagline: Multi-layered works employing non-conventional media and processes.
Biography:
James Seffens grew up in an Ohio enclave populated by his extended family. It was a DIY, grow your
own sort of place, so naturally James taught himself to paint, build, and carve. He attended OSU,
obtaining a degree in geology. Upon moving to New York City in the 1970's he met and began
working with an older sculptor, Nicolas Cortes, who had a studio in Hell's Kitchen where he produced

Island City in 2011

Tagline: Original independent artist home bound  hand paints and puts her original art on her shirts and bags
Biography:
Judith Berman
Born in New York City, Judith has lived in the Bronx, is a longtime resident of Queens, and has made art since the age of seven. Her artistic skill was recognized while she was a Brownie, and as a Girl Scout her creations such as yarn dolls earned merit badges. A self-taught artist who admires Andy Warhol, Peter Max, and Marc Chagall, she loves color, working primarily on canvas and sketch pads. She has utilized acrylic, pastel, markers, and pencil and now works exclusively in acrylic marker in vivid hues to create serene images of animals and flowers as well as abstract designs. Judith communicates and expresses her passion through artmaking, which has been instrumental in breaking barriers and in helping her to ease isolation. A daughter of Holocaust survivors, Judith has lived with trauma and depression. She is a homebound, disabled senior who finds peace and harmony through spreading joy through her art. She finds satisfaction in uploading her art images to t-shirts and totes as a means of sharing her work and creating gifts for loved ones.
Artist Statement:
I am Judith Berman and i was born in nyc.  I  began art work as a child and it was actually recognized when i was a brownie in girl scouts i used creative crafts that earned badges including creating yarn dolls 
I love art and working with colors, acrylics, pastels, markers and pencils.  I work on canvas and sketch pads using white or black. I Also do photography.  I am self taught but  also always attended art classes and photography classes.  I  love using colors and   photography depicting animals and flowers as well as abstract designs and love andy Warhol and peter max, also Chagall.  I  Love capturing life in photos including urban life and the struggles of aging.
I also love capturing photos in day to day life.
Art is a means for communication and to express my passion.  It has been instrumental in breaking through barriers and helping me  recover from isolation and communicate with others.

Tagline: Visual artist creating bold, character-driven works inspired by identity and everyday life in Queens.
Biography:
Natalie Bedon (she/her) is a queer Ecuadorian-American visual artist, cultural worker, and arts administrator based in Queens, NY. Her vivid paintings and drawings, inspired by imagined alter egos and people in her life, use bold colors to reflect the energy of those around her.

She has worked at cultural institutions, including the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), El Museo del Barrio, and The Metropolitan Museum of Art, developing public programs and large-scale cultural celebrations. 

Currently, she is the Project Manager at Flushing Town Hall, leading the Queens Cultural Mapping Project in partnership with the New York State Council on the Arts (NYSCA).

Tagline: Got that NYC grit
Biography:
Susana Aldanondo (b. 1976, Buenos Aires, Argentina) is an Argentine-American artist who lives and works in New York City. 

Working across painting, drawing, and sculpture, her practice explores abstraction in relation to music, migration, and cultural memory. Drawing on visual traditions from Buenos Aires and structures of rhythm, repetition, and improvisation, her work engages questions of identity, belonging, and translation between sound and image.

Aldanondo received an MFA from the New York Academy of Art, where she studied with Will Cotton and José de Jesús Rodríguez, and an MA in Public Art and Culture from the Universidad Nacional de las Artes, Buenos Aires. She earned a Fine Arts Diploma in Painting from The Art Students League of New York, where she studied with Larry Poons, Ronnie Landfield, and Ron Davis, and participated in seminars with Frank Stella and Knox Martin. She completed a residency at the Metropolitan Museum of Art through the New York Academy of Art, conducting research on European and American painting before joining the Museum’s copyist program. Her residencies also include the School of Visual Arts and an international residency in Iceland.

Her work has been presented in collaboration with musicians and composers affiliated with Juilliard, Columbia University, the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music, AvanTango, Suarez-Paz Tango, and Central Park Tango.
Artist Statement:
My paintings investigate the relationship between music, abstraction, and cultural memory, translating musical structure into visual form through rhythm, repetition, geometry, and color. Drawing on musical traditions shaped by migration, I use sound as both a compositional framework and a repository of history, tracing the movement of people, ideas, and identities across cultures.

Working while listening to music, I approach painting as an immersive and responsive process. Tempo, pattern, and improvisation inform the organization of the surface, allowing color, line, and symbolic forms to develop through systems of repetition and variation. The resulting works occupy a space between order and intuition, where structured compositions coexist with moments of spontaneity.

Underlying this formal language is an ongoing investigation of immigrant histories and the ways music preserves memory across generations. My work considers both the struggles of displacement and adaptation and the cultural richness that migration contributes to society.  In the face of the recent attacks on immigrants my focus has been on highlighting the history of immigration in New York, and around the world, primarily through my background as a Latin American immigrant.
Through abstraction, I seek to create spaces where these histories can be experienced through rhythm, perception, and visual resonance rather than literal narrative.

In my figurative series, I draw from ancient art and mythological archetypes while reimagining them through my own symbolic vocabulary. These works often center on female figures, or dancers, exploring the feminine perspective across history and celebrating empowerment through a contemporary lens. My recent projects expand this dialogue by delving further into unseen or metaphysical realms, often oscillating between abstraction and figuration to create narratives that feel both personal and in response with the events that are happening in our society.

Tagline: Lens-based and mixed media artist exploring post-colonial ecologies and dreamscapes.
Biography:
Raqeebah was born in Guyana, South America and double majored in Film and Cinema Studies at the University of Central Florida. She is currently based in Little Guyana, Queens, New York where she was raised for the majority of her childhood.
Her work has been displayed locally, nationally and globally at the Third Horizon Film Festival in Miami, FL, Timehri Film Festival in Guyana, Bihar Biennial in India, Jamaica Center for Arts and Learning and Jamaica Performing Arts Center in Queens, NY, the University of Maryland's Latin American and Caribbean Studies Center and more. Raqeebah was also a grant recipient of Kodak, Panavision and the Queens Art Fund.

Tagline: NYC born  artist dedicated to using public art as a tool for healing and community empowerment.
Biography:
I’m Shanice Figeroux nyc born visual and performing artist, muralist, and healing arts facilitator dedicated to creating transformative public art experiences that foster connection, resilience, and joy. With over a decade of experience activating community spaces through large scale murals, therapeutic art workshops, and grassroots collaborations, I blend bold abstract designs with social impact, using my  work as a tool for healing and empowerment particularly within communities of color, youth, and underserved neighborhoods.
My public art installations and spray painted murals are often inspired by themes of strength, unity, and emotional wellness have been featured across New York City, from public schools and healthcare centers to cultural festivals and parks. I have painted more than 20 commissioned murals and led over 123 public workshops and community art therapy events since 2021

Tagline: Rashmi is a Queens award-winning artist creating bold stories across music, film, and live performance.
Biography:
Rashmi is a Queens-based singer-songwriter, actor, and screenwriter creating bold, genre-crossing work rooted in cinematic storytelling, live performance, and emotionally charged human narratives. An AUDELCO-nominated actress, her performance work spans classical theatre, contemporary drama, comedy, and independent film, including collaborations with Ron Howard, Target Margin Theater, the New York Fringe Festival, and the Classical Theatre Lab. Alongside her acting work, she creates original music blending global influences, sharp lyrical writing, and strong melodic hooks shaped by the cultural intersections of New York City.

A recipient of the 2026 NYFA Queens Artist Award for new work, Rashmi is currently developing her feature screenplay FARE TRADE, an action-comedy set in Queens around the NYC taxi industry and predatory lending crisis. She is also a former Writers Guild of America East x FilmNation Screenwriting Fellow and Baldwin Fellow.

Across music, film, theatre, and live performance, Rashmi’s work centers emotionally resonant storytelling that brings people together across cultures and generations. She has performed as part of the International Human Rights Arts Festival, written and performed original work at Tribeca Performing Arts Center, and continues to develop new interdisciplinary work inspired by the energy, breadth, and shared humanity of New York City

Tagline: A performing artist who specializes in Indian Classical dance exploring both traditional and contemporary narratives.
Biography:
I am an immigrant who arrived in this country nine years ago. Raised in South India, I began my journey in Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi under my mother's guidance before advancing my training with renowned gurus in India. Having found community and purpose in New York City through the arts, I am deeply committed to enriching the city's cultural landscape. Indian classical dance serves as a powerful medium for sharing the rich narratives and philosophies of my heritage—such as yoga, mindfulness, and breathwork—bringing these ancient traditions to a broader, contemporary audience.

I have widely performed across India and the US at prestigious venues like the Lincoln Center, India International Center, 92StY, and famed festivals such as Drive East, Battery Dance, Making Moves Dance Festival . I have also conducted dance workshops for students at the American Ballet Theater, 92StY, exposing them to the technique and discipline of Indian classical dance. I have served as a teaching artist, introducing my art form to New York City public school students, and served as an Arts Program Manager, combining my experience as a performer and educator to help various NY public schools meet their arts education needs.
Artist Statement: Aishwarya Madhav is an Indian classical dancer and an Arts educator. She is an emerging artist known for her striking footwork and her storytelling expertise. An emerging artist with a distinctive stage presence, her work brings clarity and emotional nuance to both traditional and contemporary narratives.

Tagline: Multidisciplinary artist exploring motherhood, grief, and transformation.
Biography: Shushanik Karapetyan is a New York-based artist born in Yerevan, Armenia. Her work has been exhibited at venues such as the National Association of Women Artists, Governors Island, BRIC, LIC Arts Open, Site: Brooklyn Gallery, Atamian Hovsepian Curatorial Practice, and Brooklyn Waterfront Artist Coalition. Shushanik has held solo exhibitions including In Between Horizons (2026),  Land Sea Sky at Yant Art Space (2025), Paintings on the Sunnyside at Vital Arts Studios Gallery (2024), and Sunsets 1–4 at Little Window Gallery (2024), all in New York. She was an exhibitor at The Other Art Fair in New York in 2025 and received the 2025 Queens Arts Fund New Work Grant from the New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) and the Queens Council on the Arts.
Artist Statement: Drawing from her practice as a Gestalt psychotherapist, Shushanik Karapetyan approaches painting with an emphasis on attunement and responsiveness to personal experience and the environment. Shushanik is inspired by color, cycles of life, and states of transition such as sunsets and seasonal changes. She is drawn to the shifting hues of sunsets and the vivid tones of flowers encountered on her walks. These impressions weave into her paintings. Her writing explores themes of motherhood, grief, and transformation and has been published in JMWW, Vines Magazine and The North Central Review.

Tagline: Urban visual artist
Biography:
Nelson Host Santiago is a Puerto Rican visual artist whose work blends narrative painting, cultural memory, and urban vibrancy. Born and raised in New York City, Santiago’s art reflects the dual identity of life between the island and the mainland, weaving together the textures, colors, and stories of both worlds. His paintings often center on themes of migration, resilience, and community, drawing inspiration from oral histories, historical archives, and his own lived experience.
With a background in large-scale painting and community-based projects, Santiago has developed a practice that is as much about cultural preservation as it is about artistic expression. His work has been exhibited in local galleries, cultural centers, and public spaces, engaging audiences through storytelling and visual immersion.
Beyond the canvas, Santiago is committed to making art accessible, leading workshops and public programs that invite people of all ages to share and celebrate their heritage. Through his projects, he aims to honor the past, amplify underrepresented narratives, and create spaces where art becomes a catalyst for connection, dialogue, and pride.

Tagline: Musician and composer blending Indian classical and Western music through performance, composition, and collaboration.
Biography:
Thakur Chakrapani Singh is an Indian musician, composer, educator, and cultural entrepreneur dedicated to the preservation and promotion of Indian classical music. He is the Founder of the Art & Cultural Trust of India (ACT), a charitable organization established to nurture Indian classical music among children, youth, and aspiring artists through the traditional Guru–Shishya Parampara. An internationally award-winning artist, Singh has released numerous solo and collaborative music albums. Among his  celebrated works are The Flavor of Strings  with French Guitarist Philippe Loli and the internationally recognized Chakra Suite, created in collaboration with acclaimed American composer Alex Shapiro. Their groundbreaking project seamlessly blends Indian classical music with contemporary Western composition and electronic soundscapes, earning international recognition and broadcasts on radio stations in the United States.
Driven by a vision to make classical music accessible to future generations, Singh has organized concerts, workshops, seminars, competitions, and training programs that provide emerging artists with opportunities to learn from and perform alongside distinguished musicians. As a performer and composer, Thakur Chakrapani Singh explores the creative dialogue between Indian classical and Western musical traditions, developing works that respect the depth of classical heritage while embracing contemporary artistic collaboration. His practice reflects a commitment to cultural exchange, education, and innovation, fostering meaningful connections between diverse musical traditions and audiences worldwide.
Through his performances, compositions, and educational initiatives, Thakur Chakrapani Singh continues to inspire musicians and audiences while advancing the global appreciation of Indian classical music.
Artist Statement:
My artistic practice is rooted in the rich traditions of Indian classical music while embracing the possibilities of cross-cultural collaboration. As a musician and composer, I seek to create meaningful conversations between Indian and Western musical traditions, bringing together diverse sounds, techniques, and perspectives without losing the integrity of either form.
Through performance, composition, and collaborative projects, I explore how music can transcend cultural boundaries and connect people across different backgrounds. I draw inspiration from the depth, discipline, and expressive power of Indian classical music, while engaging with contemporary musical ideas and global influences to create works that are both rooted in tradition and open to innovation.
My work reflects a commitment to preserving musical heritage while expanding its reach through creative exchange. By combining tradition with experimentation, I aim to create performances and compositions that celebrate cultural diversity, encourage dialogue, and demonstrate music's ability to build shared understanding across communities.

Tagline: Visual artist exploring the relationship of matter and spirit.
Biography: Karen Fitzgerald was born and raised on a dairy farm in the Midwest. It is this early, close relationship with the natural world that informs her work. This work has been actively exhibited in the United States.  The Queens Museum of Art, Fort Wayne Museum of Art, Islip Art Museum, Rahr-West Museum, Madison Art Museum, Milwaukee Art Museum, Milwaukee Institute of Art & Design, the University of Arizona – Tucson and the United Nations in NYC have featured her work in their active exhibition schedules.  She received grants from the Queens Community Arts Fund, the Greenwall Foundation, the New York Foundation for the Arts, and the Women’s Studio Workshop.  Her work is in many private and public collections, including the Spencer Collection of the New York Public Library, Related Group, the Rienhart Collection of Germany, Montefiore Medical Center, NYU Langone Medical Center, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, NYC; the Fort Wayne Museum of Art, Rahr-West Art Museum and special collections at Princeton, Berkeley, and College of William and Mary.
Artist Statement:
The relationship of matter and spirit is at the heart of my work. The physicality of the earth is tangible and real. Another dimension is indelibly linked to that materiality, one that is experienced though it cannot be measured or delineated. That elusive relationship between matter and spirit has been explored extensively in verbal form—poetry, philosophy, metaphysics—and those texts are essential touchstones in my work. Finding forms to translate that awareness into visual language is an essential commitment in my work.

I use fluid media—watercolor, thinned oil paint, mica. These layered surfaces are luminous and subtle. This way of working demands that I step back from my intentionality and trust the process, giving voice to the materials I am using. I incorporate gilding with precious metals as a way of adding to the “other worldly” quality I am seeking.

The language of form in these paintings connects the dots to the spiritual realm through the energy of all things physical. Energy is the bridge between the physical and the spiritual. Light, particularly, calls our senses to the presence of that which is metaphysical. This work is making space for the voice of spirit.

Tagline: Ecuadorian Illustrator & Oil painter based in NYC, specializing in colorful genre paintings and editorial illustrations.
Biography:
I am an Ecuadorian Photographer and Illustrator based in Queens, New York. 
In observing quiet, ordinary moments, I am driven to capture everyday life through bright colors and lively narratives that explore themes of community, nature and the way identity is shaped by our surroundings. I am inspired by daily observations of working people. By using a vibrant color palette, the attention is set on people who are often overlooked, illustrating their dignity and reminding the audience of the integrity in their labor. Whether it’s a portrait of a person from the community or a scene illustrating a neighborhood’s landscape, I aspire to capture identity and personality, both in people and places.
Artist Statement:
My love for art and illustration derives from a personal connection to images from an early age. Having moved to the United States from Ecuador, I faced a language barrier which made me realize how universal and powerful the visual world is. Despite not being able to understand the language, I understood the language of art and connected with it. 
As I quietly observed ordinary moments, my interest was sparked to create colorful genre paintings and lively narratives that explore themes of community, nature and identity. Inspired by daily observations of working people, their labor, as well as a connection to nature on regular walks, I set out to document everyday life. Through the use of a vibrant color palette, the attention is set on people who are often overlooked, illustrating their dignity and reminding the audience of the integrity in their labor.

Tagline: Mixed media artist creating biomorphic worlds where feeling, body, and nature become forms of reflection and rest.
Artist Statement: My work explores the relationship between the body, nervous system, and natural world. Through mixed media, printmaking, sculpture, and installation, I create biomorphic forms that resemble organisms, symbols, fossils, and emotional fragments. Rooted in ideas of inner ecology, rest, and regulation, my practice considers how feelings become shapes and how nature can help us return to ourselves.

Tagline: Poet and cultural worker exploring language, place, and public space through writing and social practice.
Biography: KC Trommer (she/her) is a poet and cultural worker in New York City. Her books include We Call Them Beautiful (Diode Editions, 2019) and The Hasp Tongue (Dancing Girl Press, 2014). A finalist for the role of Queens Poet Laureate, KC is the founder and curator of QUEENSBOUND, an ongoing public poetry series on the 7 train (queensbound.com). Throughout her career she has been the recipient of an Academy of American Poets Prize, the Diode Editions Book Prize, a Fugue Poetry Prize, as well as grants and fellowships from City Artist Corps, the New York Foundation for the Arts, NYPL’s Cullman Center, Onassis USA, and the Lower Manhattan Cultural Council, amongst others. KC has taught courses in creative writing at the University of Michigan, NYU, Bard, and Poets House. Since 2018, KC has collaborated with the Grammy Award-winning composer Herschel Garfein on a song cycle based on poems from her first collection, three of which were included in Garfein’s 2023 classical music release The Layers. She holds a BA in English from the University of Georgia, and an MFA in Poetry from the University of Michigan Helen Zell Writers’ Program. She lives in Jackson Heights, Queens, with her son. Learn more at kctrommer.com.

Tagline: Arab musician and educator
Biography:
One of the leading Arab violinists in the U.S., as well as a vocalist, Sami Abu Shumays is internationally known as a master of the maqam system. He is co-author of the acclaimed book Inside Arabic Music (Oxford University Press 2019), and his passion for teaching and oral tradition is also expressed through his YouTube series "Maqam Lessons," the website www.maqamlessons.com, and his contributions to www.maqamworld.com. Co-founder and director of the NYC-based Arabic music and dance ensemble Zikrayat, Sami released his first solo album Circles in 2023, available on all streaming platforms. In 2024 he was named a master folk artist through the New York State Council on the Arts Folk Arts Apprenticeship Program. In 2024 he was also awarded one of 25 Taproot fellowships nationally for folk artists rooted in communities, by the Alliance for California Traditional Arts. He is an advisory board member of Brooklyn Maqam, the organization promoting the largest number of Arabic music events in NYC, and Deputy Director at Flushing Town Hall, a multi-disciplinary arts presenter based in Queens, NY.

Sami has led Zikrayat since 2005, which has been featured at GlobalFEST, numerous venues in New York City and nationwide. Zikrayat has recorded two albums: Live At Lotus (which won a 2008 Independent Music Award) and Cinematic. 

A second-generation Palestinian-American, Sami originally studied Western music before traveling to the Arab World to reconnect with his roots. He studied with Alfred Gamil in Cairo; Mohamed Qasas, Abdel-Basit Bakkar, and Abdel-Minaim Senkary in Aleppo; and Simon Shaheen and Yusuf Kassab in New York. Sami has a bachelor’s degree in Western music theory and composition from Harvard University, several years of graduate work in composition and ethnomusicology at the CUNY Graduate Center, and received a Fulbright Fellowship to study Arabic music and language in Cairo, Egypt.

Tagline: Performance collective to redefine center and periphery
Biography:
in-version ensemble is a performance collective founded in 2024 by a shared mission to redefine center and periphery. We amplify female, queer, and AAPI narratives through ensemble-based works rooted in collaboration, research, and audience interaction. 

We have received support from the NYSCA, LMCC, Queens Arts Fund, and Broadway Green Alliance. Our works have been nominated by Asian Arts Award Scotland at the 2024 Edinburgh Fringe Festival, Spirit of the Fest Award at the 2025 Hollywood Fringe Festival, and the 2025 BroadwayWorld Off-Broadway Awards. We are the organizer of ChuanFest, the annual survey of Asian contemporary performance.
Artist Statement:
in-version ensemble develops, produces original performances collectively, through the cultivation of trust, sincerity, and joy. We make art we need now. 
 
in-version ensemble is curious about the plasticity of human interactions. We investigate identity and relationships while embracing the tensions between languages–written, spoken, improvised, digital, movements. 

We aim to redefine center and periphery.
We probe the construction of self and narrative within foreign, innovative spaces.

Tagline: Painter, sculptor, animator forging spontaneous outbursts of energy.
Biography: Elliot Cowan is an Australian multidisciplinary artist who makes lots of cowboys, abstracts and barnyard animals. His work has been showcased all over the world. He enjoys nothing more than making things and talking about them over bourbon and vodkas. He loves living and working in Queens, The World's Borough.

Tagline: Jazz vocalist, composer, and bandleader bringing the Great American Songbook and original music to new audiences.
Biography:
Hyeonseon Baek is a Korean jazz vocalist, composer, and bandleader based in New York City. A graduate of the New England Conservatory, he performs the Great American Songbook alongside original compositions rooted in the straight-ahead jazz tradition.

His debut album, Longing, features Kevin Hays, Linda May Han Oh, Jochen Rueckert, and Lucas Pino. Baek has performed at venues including Five Spot Jazz, Pangea, Kato Sake Works, ShapeShifter Lab, and Birdland’s The Lineup and Cast Party series.

He is a 2026 New York State Council on the Arts (NYSCA) Artist Grant recipient and previously received support from the Queens Arts Fund before being invited to serve as a 2026 Queens Arts Fund panelist. Through performance, composition, and community engagement, he is committed to expanding the reach of jazz while fostering meaningful connections across audiences.
Artist Statement:
My work explores jazz as a living language that crosses cultural and generational boundaries. As a Korean jazz vocalist based in New York City, I interpret the Great American Songbook and bebop tradition through my own experiences of migration, memory, and identity.

Through original compositions and reimagined standards, I aim to connect the history of jazz with contemporary audiences. My performances focus on storytelling, improvisation, swing, and emotional honesty, creating a space where tradition and personal narrative can meet.

Tagline: Interdisciplinary artist
Biography:
Maria Flores is a Mexican-American artist, born and raised in Queens, New York. Flores, also known as Lágrimas, previously pursued a career in health professions and shifted towards visual arts during the COVID-19 pandemic. Flores is a recent graduate with a BFA in Studio Arts from Queens College. In 2024, she completed the Arts and Leadership bootcamp. She was awarded the Tana and Matisse and the Select Fund award. She was nominated for the Yale/Norfolk School of Arts 2025 summer program by Queens College. 
     During her academic journey, Flores worked with art institutions as an intern, teaching artist, and exhibiting artist.  In 2025, she worked with Emmy nominee Anthony Rojas for the NYLFF campaign commercial as a set dresser and brand ambassador. In the fall of 2025, Flores interned with CUNY Cultural Corps as a production management intern. She was selected to work with Brooklyn Ballet for their Brooklyn Nutcracker production. As a fine artist, she has exhibited in Queens, Southampton, Brooklyn, and Manhattan. Her most notable and recent exhibition at Ma's House & BIPOC Art Studio features her work in the published book "Reclaiming Death". This summer, she taught painting and sketching classes with Arts in the Parks. Previously, she led Carving with Plaster classes at Art Retail Therapy.
Artist Statement: Maria utilizes performance, video, and sculpture to create installation-like work relating to family dynamics and alcoholism. Her work displaces nightlife objects to question and define the relationship between substance and culture. Themes of grief, hope, and mercy are incorporated to create a digestible work. Flores repeatedly reframes and decontextualizes celebratory moments to address and assess the role alcohol plays in an individual.

Tagline: Multidisciplinary artist and theater maker exploring storytelling through performance, curation, and community work.
Biography:
Xtian Ávila serves as the Executive and Artistic Associate at Flushing Town Hall, where he supports the institution’s mission of cultural exchange. A curator, theatre maker, teaching artist, and Drama League Fellow, Xtian is also the founder and Co-Artistic Director of MexFest, a project dedicated to celebrating and amplifying contemporary Mexican voices. 
With a background in directing, producing, playwriting and performing, Xtian has collaborated with The Public Theater and curated community-focused festivals at The Tank NYC. His recent theatrical work includes The Sun Serpent and Elephant & Piggie’s “We are in a Play!” at the Hangar Theatre, as well as productions of Romeo & Juliet and Twelfth Night at New York Live Arts. 
After a career spent building a foundation in luxury hospitality management at such storied destinations as The Setai, The Fairmont, and The Lowell, Xtian is honored to now dedicate his professional life to his lifelong passion for the arts. 
Deeply committed to service, Xtian is a yoga instructor and a Board Member of GLC (Gay Latino Collective). He has found his most meaningful fulfillment through advocacy for indigenous populations with The God’s Child Project and supporting families in marginalized neighborhoods of Guatemala City with Camino Seguro. Xtian is inspired by the power of the arts to build bridges and is honored to contribute to his vibrant community in New York City. He lives in Harlem with his miniature-pinscher, Rico.

Tagline: Visual Artist/Illustrator capturing overlooked objects and people through the use of soft and delicate line work.
Biography: Melissa Velasquez is a Colombian-American illustrator from Queens, New York. Her work captures overlooked objects, people, and fleeting moments through the use of soft and delicate line work. Primarily creating warm drawings on paper, she is interested in exploring beauty in the mundane and honoring the solace found in the longing for human connection.

Tagline: Visual Artist and Curator exploring identity & migration through the lens of women using mixed media work.
Biography:
Seema Shakti is a NYC-based Visual Artist/Curator, Educator, and Cultural Worker who was born in the Bronx and grew up in the Little Guyana neighborhood of Queens, NYC. She currently lives and works in Queens on occupied Canarsie/Munsee Lenape land.

Seema is the founder of Coolitude Arts Collective for Indo-Caribbean-identifying artists and an artist member of the South Asian Womxn’s Creative Collective, LIC-A, and Southeast Queens Artist Alliance.

She has presented her work at Jamaica Center for Arts & Learning (JCAL), King Manor Museum, Flushing Town Hall, Square’s HQ, and The School District of Philadelphia’s HQ. She was the 2021 recipient of the New York City Artist Corps grant.

Her curatorial work as an inaugural Visual Voices Curator (2023- 2025) at Jamaica Center for Arts & Learning (JCAL) amplified local BIIPOC creatives in Queens and NYC. She most recently curated In Community With The Land (2024-25) and Ancestral Nourishment (2023-24), two group exhibitions that collectively featured the works of over thirty artists of diverse backgrounds from the five boroughs of New York City.

She holds 15+ years of experience as an educator within the youth development sector in the nonprofit world with experience in facilitation, curriculum development, program management & design.
Artist Statement: As a South Asian and Indo-Caribbean artist, Seema explores identity, migration and ancestry through her mixed media work. She views her art practice as a nourishing ritual meditation that connects her to her ancestors, kundalini shakti, and the cosmos. Her work incorporates elements of magical realism like third eyes that serve as a portal that connects the women she depicts in her work to their ancestral truth and power.

Tagline: A speculative and experimental Afro-Caribbean-American poet and interdisciplinary artist
Biography:
Sherese Francis (she/they) describes themselves as an AlkyMist of the I-Magination, finding expression through poetry, interdisciplinary arts (collage, book and paper arts, sound and performance art), workshop facilitation, editing, and literary curation. Her(e) work takes inspiration from her(e) Afro-Caribbean heritage (Barbados and Dominica), and studies in Afrofuturism and Black Speculative Arts, mythology and etymology. Some of their work has been published in Women’s Studies Quarterly, Furious Flower, Obsidian, Rootwork Journal, The Caribbean Writer, The Operating System, Cosmonauts Avenue, No Dear, Apex Magazine, Bone Bouquet, African Voices, Newtown Literary, and Free Verse. Additionally, Sherese has published four chapbooks, Lucy’s Bone Scrolls (Three Legged Elephant, 2017), Variations on Sett/ling Seed/ling (Harlequin Creature, 2018), Recycling a Why That Rules Over My Sacred Sight (DoubleCross Press, 2021) and Lady Liberty Smashing Stones (THRASH Press, 2022), and edited a poetry anthology/guided journal, Baby Suggs and a Purple Butterfly (Get Fresh Books, 2024). Sherese won Inverted Syntax’s 2024 Aggrey Book Prize for Poetry for PollyNation: A Seminary of Self, which will be published in 2027.

Sherese has received grants and awards from Queens Council on the Arts, NYFA, NYSCA and The Caribbean Writer, residencies from the NY Aquarium, WorksonWater, LMCC, Akademie Schloss Solitude and SeaSalted Honey in Senegal, and fellowships from Voodoonauts, Baldwin for the Arts and Anaphora Arts. Besides publications, Sherese has had her(e) work featured in various exhibitions and showcases from LMCC Gallery on Governors Island, NY Aquarium, NY Live Arts, Queens Public Library, York College Arts Gallery, King Manor Museum, WorksOnWater, Flushing Town Hall, Jamaica Center for Arts & Learning, Bliss On Bliss, Maleza Proyectos, Flux Factory, The Rubenstein Art Center, The Loomis Chaffee School Mercy Gallery, and Ely Center for Contemporary Art.

Artist Statement: I am a speculative and experimental poet and interdisciplinary artist open to working with any medium that piques my interest. Within the past decade, I have worked with collage (physical and digital), assemblage (collage with objects), book arts, paper art, sound art and performance art. I also do social practice, community activation work and workshop/lab facilitation, working with local community groups, like the Southeast Queens Artist Alliance, Newtown Literary and the spoken word/poetry subway project, Queensbound, as well as cultural organizations like the Lewis Latimer House Museum, King Manor Museum, York College fine and performing arts department and Queens Public Library to create programming for my community. My work is largely inspired by Afrofuturism and Black Speculative Arts and some of the themes in my work have included history of places in Southeast Queens, history of the African diaspora, intersections between art, culture and science, Black people in science, creation of altar and ritual objects, language and writing as visual art, poetry as scientific language, radio poetry, mobile libraries, recycled art, environmental art, and memory work. I consider what I do I kind of speculative and sacred knowledge making and knowledge preservation.

Tagline: Painter open to Collaboration and new forms of play
Biography: Born and raised in New York City, I am a self-taught painter whose work reflects the raw emotion and layered complexity of urban life and human connection. With a background in fashion, I bring a unique sensitivity to texture, color, and form—infusing each canvas with a visceral, tactile quality that blurs the line between visual art and lived experience.
Artist Statement:
Though not classically trained, my intuitive approach to painting is deeply personal and unfiltered. Drawing inspiration from the people, struggles, and silences of everyday life, my work explores themes of identity, and emotional presence.

Rooted in the energy and grit of the city, my art resists polish in favor of honesty. My creative practice is an act of observation and empathy—an attempt to capture what words often can’t.

Tagline: Artist couple exploring the world together with their own unique style.
Biography: Ardlee and Aaron Simon have lived in Queens, NY, all their lives.  They have been married for 21 years and have 2 kids. Unknowingly, they have had a love for art since they were children.  Each in their own way, has been drawing since they were children.  Aaron was always interested in cartoons and anime, and Ardlee was always fascinated by faces. They both have a BA in Fine Arts, concentrating on their respective branches.  Aaron graduated in cartooning and Ardlee at that time, in Fashion.

Tagline: Hand-stitched art about connection, community, womanhood, and the tenderness of humanity.
Biography: Emily Pavacic is a Queens-based visual artist, dancer, and educator whose artistic career has been shaped by her dual passions for the visual arts and dance. Emily earned her Bachelor of Fine Arts from Adelphi University. Upon graduating, she continued her studies and earned a Masters in Art Education from NYU- the prelude to a 9-year public school-teaching career.  Inspired by commonality within the human experience and deep connections, her work is often described as tender and intricate. Emily resides in Queens, NY with her husband and their three cats.

Work Samples.filename: The Universal Threads That Connect Us_1.jpg

Artist Statement: As humans, we have only inhabited this planetary body for about 0.007% of the lifespan of earth- a blink in the cosmos. Despite our brevity as a species, our experiences feel significant. My work explores universality within the human experience and its ephemerality. I seek to create work about contemplation, struggle, community, healing, deep connections, aging as a woman, community, and times of celebration. My pieces consist of labor-intensive and meditative hand-stitched drawings on textiles. Often, these works incorporate the use of paint, multiple layers of fabric for dimensionality, and eco-printing with flowers grown on my balcony. My artwork is gestural and expressive, informed by my years of training and performing as a dancer.

Tagline: Singer-participate in preservation of Ukrainian culture, heritage and ethnic traditions of Ukrainians around the world.
Biography: Natalia Maslak - singer, musician, performer with extensive experience. Performed and directed different kinds of musical events across different genres such as Pop, World, Soul, Folk, Rock. Tagline: Socially engaged artist and community organizer working in areas around Flushing Bay and Flushing Creek
Biography:
Cody Herrmann is an artist and community organizer based in Queens, New York. She combines socially engaged art, political advocacy, and community science to create participatory art works and public programs. Guided by her interest in public space and urban resilience Cody’s work explores urban planning processes while applying an iterative, human centered approach to ecological problem solving. Since 2014 her work has focused on her hometown of Flushing, creating projects critiquing policy related to land use and environmental planning in areas surrounding Flushing Bay and Flushing Creek, primarily through small scale urban design interventions and guided tours.

Cody has been the recipient of the Space to Connect: Chashama Teaching Artist Residency, apexart International Fellowship, Culture Push Climate Justice Fellowship, Human Impacts Institute Impact Artist Fellowship, More Art Engaging Artists Fellowship, Jamaica Center for Arts and Learning Artist in Residency Fellowship, and Works on Water Residency. Cody holds an MFA from Social Practice Queens at CUNY Queens College, and undergraduate degree from Parsons School of Design.

A Glimpse of the Future (its bound to come tumbling down)

Artist Statement:
Climate change and environmental degradation are impacting communities at increasing rates across the globe. The institutionalized walls blocking ecological subjects and environmental justice from being understood and acted upon by the general population must be broken down to ensure human adaptation and a resilient future. My work references municipal policy and local history, highlighting site-specific relationships between land use, and both individual and institutional agency, disrupting traditional notions of artistic authorship, labor, and institutional expertise.

Drawing from my background in ecology and urban design, my works are informed by a combination of site visits, qualitative research, secondary research, in-context immersion, and self-reflection. Manifesting primarily as onsite interventions, performance, guided tours, and public workshops, my projects often address public access, urban planning processes, and civic participation. 

Inspired by human centered design methods I have chosen to focus much of my work in my hometown of Flushing, Queens. For over ten years I have studied Flushing Bay and Flushing Creek to further explore my interests in public space, ecology, and urban development. This ongoing series of socially engaged work has led me to collaborate with numerous institutions, individuals, and advocacy groups working locally.
